facts.note: Matthey's question places the watch inspection when the temple bell struck nine; Vauthier confirms Aurèle had them show watches and that his own was two minutes ahead of the bell.

Piquet with Madame (Odile) in the salon until a quarter to eleven by his watch; he went out to the hall to fetch his cigar case from his coat; piano began as he went out and stopped when he came back.
He sat down again and the hall clock struck eleven a moment after he did.

added.quote: the regulator stopped with its master
added.why: Claims the atelier regulator stopped at the moment Aurèle died, so a detective could tie the death to a clock-stop time and treat the two as simultaneous. Its reading is not given, so it yields a relation, not a clock reading.
